comments.author: @cosmic-minds-origin
comments.text: Worth adding that New Zealand was not the only one in the room. The 1890 conference that began all this was Australasian, not Australian, and Fiji was represented at the earlier Australasian meetings too. The federation that formed was the subset that stayed, which is why the name on the 1900 Act is the Commonwealth of Australia rather than anything wider.

comments.author: @cosmic-minds-origin
comments.text: The sharper half of this is what happened to the seats nobody mentions. The constitution still allows Parliament to admit new states, and in more than a century it never has. The Northern Territory, which is inside Australia and wanted it, put statehood to its own voters in 1998 and they said no. So the document keeps a place open for a country that declined across 2,000 km of sea, while a territory that asked has been sitting in the waiting room since 1911.
